body:
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/NGP/NGP13/1/87444/images/New%20Sewell%20Delegate%20Logo%20.png]
Session Week 2 Newsletter
Hello neighbors,
The second week of the General Assembly session is wrapping up, and I want to update you on what’s taking place in Richmond.
Committee Assignments
As I mentioned in my prior message, I’m proud to represent our district on four committees in the House of Delegates: Appropriations [https://lis.virginia.gov/cgi-bin/legp604.exe?241+com+H2] , Education [https://lis.virginia.gov/cgi-bin/legp604.exe?241+com+H9] , Transportation [https://lis.virginia.gov/cgi-bin/legp604.exe?241+com+H19] , and Counties Cities and Towns [https://lis.virginia.gov/cgi-bin/legp604.exe?241+com+H7] .
Additionally, I’ll be chairing the following subcommittees:
The House Education Subcommittee on Higher Education [https://lis.virginia.gov/cgi-bin/legp604.exe?241+sub+H09002]
The House Transportation Subcommittee on the Department of Motor Vehicles [https://lis.virginia.gov/cgi-bin/legp604.exe?241+sub+H19001]
The House Counties, Cities and Towns Subcommittee #2 [https://lis.virginia.gov/cgi-bin/legp604.exe?241+sub+H07002]
Each of these committee and subcommittee assignments is an opportunity for me to be your voice as we consider critical pieces of legislation and debate policies that will impact the lives of residents of Prince William County and all across the Commonwealth.
Welcome to Richmond! Visits, Constituent Meetings & More
These last two weeks, I have had the pleasure of meeting some of my constituents here in Richmond, welcoming several advocacy organizations, and speaking with different groups during their lobby days. Thank you so much for taking the time to stop by, for sharing your feedback, and for being so active and engaged. Your participation is crucial to our democracy, and I thank you for your ongoing commitment to improving our shared Commonwealth.
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/NGP/NGP13/1/87444/images/Screenshot%202024-01-19%20at%207.38.52%20AM.png] I met with representatives from the Medical Society of Virginia [https://www.msv.org/] . Thanks so much for stopping by!
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/NGP/NGP13/1/87444/images/Screenshot%202024-01-19%20at%207.39.01%20AM.png] Prince William County representatives from Moms Demand Action [https://momsdemandaction.org/virginia-moms-demand-action-students-demand-action-volunteers-gather-to-meet-with-lawmakers-for-advocacy-day-on-capitol-square/] visited my office to discuss efforts to pass common sense legislation to reduce gun violence and keep our communities safe.
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/NGP/NGP13/1/87444/images/Screenshot%202024-01-19%20at%207.39.18%20AM.png] I had the opportunity to speak to members of the Northern Virginia Chamber of Commerce [https://novachamber.org/] during their lobby day.
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/NGP/NGP13/1/87444/images/Screenshot%202024-01-19%20at%207.39.32%20AM.png] My staff welcomed members of SkillsUSA [https://www.skillsusa.org/] to our office to discuss workforce preparation and efforts to support skills training, trades, and career readiness for students.
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/NGP/NGP13/1/87444/images/Screenshot%202024-01-19%20at%207.39.42%20AM.png] Members of my staff and I attended the Governor’s reception at the Governor’s Mansion to kick off the 2024 General Assembly Session.
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/NGP/NGP13/1/87444/images/Screenshot%202024-01-19%20at%207.39.54%20AM.png] Fellow Delegate Mike Jones joined me to to speak with the local Kappa League [https://therac1945.com/guide-right/] , a program for young men aged 13 to 18, sponsored by the Kappa Alpha Psi [https://therac1945.com/] fraternity. It was an honor to address these young leaders during Kappa Legislative Day!
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/NGP/NGP13/1/87444/images/Screenshot%202024-01-19%20at%207.40.05%20AM.png] I had the privilege of welcoming President Rowe [https://www.wm.edu/about/administration/president/] from the College of William and Mary to my office! As the Chair of the House Higher Education Subcommittee, it was a pleasure to discuss access, affordability, and preparing our students for the future with her.
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/NGP/NGP13/1/87444/images/Screenshot%202024-01-19%20at%207.40.15%20AM.png] Many thanks to the members of the Virginia Bankers Association [https://www.vabankers.org/] for stopping by my office to share their legislative agenda.
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/NGP/NGP13/1/87444/images/Screenshot%202024-01-19%20at%207.40.24%20AM.png] I was glad to meet with representatives from Justice Forward Virginia [https://justiceforwardva.com/] to discuss critical criminal justice issues facing the Commonwealth.
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/NGP/NGP13/1/87444/images/CareInAction.png] While I don’t have a photo with the group, I would like to thank the representatives from Care in Action [https://careinaction.us/about/] who visited my office where to discussed the needs of Virginia’s domestic workers and how we can better protect and support this vital part of our workforce.
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/NGP/NGP13/1/87444/images/IMG_0016.jpg] I was happy to meet members of The National Emergency Number Association [https://www.nena.org/] (NENA) and to talk about issues that face 911 operators and our public safety system.
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/NGP/NGP13/1/87444/images/IMG_0031.jpg] Thanks to members of the VFW and the Joint Leadership Council [https://www.dvs.virginia.gov/dvs/joint-leadership-council-veterans-service-organizations-2] of veteran service organizations who have worked with our office on several veterans protections bills.
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/NGP/NGP13/1/87444/images/IMG_0034.jpg] I heard directly from members of the 40strong [https://the40strong.com/] movement about the conditions in our criminal justice system.
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/NGP/NGP13/1/87444/images/IMG_0041.jpg] I was joined by members of CASA [https://wearecasa.org/about/] to talk about the importance of minimum wage and protections for workers.
Legislative Actions Which Impact You
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/NGP/NGP13/1/87444/images/Screenshot%202024-01-19%20at%207.40.33%20AM.png] As a member of the House Transportation Committee, I participated in this week’s meeting as we gear up to review hundreds of bills. You can see which bills are currently before the committee here [https://lis.virginia.gov/cgi-bin/legp604.exe?241+com+H19] .
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/NGP/NGP13/1/87444/images/IMG_0030.jpg] As a delegate who represents a district where 1 in 6 people is a veteran or armed service member, I’m a proud member of the House Veterans and Military Caucus. The caucus met this week to discuss bills before the general assembly which affect service members, veterans, and their families. During the meeting, the caucus discussed my bill, HB 736 [https://lis.virginia.gov/cgi-bin/legp604.exe?241+sum+HB736] , which seeks to protect veterans from claim sharks who take advantage of veterans with false benefits guarantees and predatory profit sharing contracts.
Bills and Subcommittees
If you’re interested in tracking certain legislation, did you know you can use the Lobbyist-in-a-Box [https://lis.virginia.gov/h015.htm] service online? This is a service provided by the Virginia Legislative Information System (LIS) that lets you track up to five bills for free. Using this link [https://vi.virginiainteractive.org/cgi-bin/liab_signup.cgi] , you can set up a free profile which will request whichever user ID and password you like, as well as your first and last name and your email address. You’ll receive a confirmation email so you can activate your account. There is a helpful FAQ at the bottom of the LIAB homepage here [https://lis.virginia.gov/h015.htm] .
You can also watch a livestream of the House while it’s in session here [https://virginiageneralassembly.gov/house/chamber/chamberstream.php] . View meetings currently in process by selecting “now playing” or watch recordings of committee and subcommittee meetings from previous days by selecting “recordings.” On this website, you can also see which committee and subcommittee meetings are in process or have adjourned. Please tune in to follow along as members of the House debate and discuss the issues that matter most to you!
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/NGP/NGP13/1/87444/images/IMG_0039.jpg]
Speaking of subcommittee meetings, I chaired the Counties Cities and Towns subcommittee on Thursday. We discussed the following bills and took the following actions:
HB147 [https://lis.virginia.gov/cgi-bin/legp604.exe?241+cab+HC10112HB0147+BREF] - passed the bill
HB128 [https://lis.virginia.gov/cgi-bin/legp604.exe?241+sum+HB128] - passed the bill
HB170 [https://lis.virginia.gov/cgi-bin/legp604.exe?241+sum+HB170] - passed the bill
HB334 [https://lis.virginia.gov/cgi-bin/legp604.exe?241+sum+HB334] - passed the bill
HB344 [https://lis.virginia.gov/cgi-bin/legp604.exe?241+sum+HB344] - did not pass the bill
HB364 [https://lis.virginia.gov/cgi-bin/legp604.exe?241+sum+HB364] - referred the bill to the General Laws Committee [https://lis.virginia.gov/cgi-bin/legp604.exe?241+com+H11]
HB405 [https://lis.virginia.gov/cgi-bin/legp604.exe?241+sum+HB405] - passed by for later discussion
HB459 [https://lis.virginia.gov/cgi-bin/legp604.exe?241+sum+HB459] - passed the bill
HB281 [https://lis.virginia.gov/cgi-bin/legp604.exe?241+sum+HB281] - passed the bill
HB456 [https://lis.virginia.gov/cgi-bin/legp604.exe?241+sum+HB456] - passed the bill
Delegates presented their bills, and we invited feedback both for and against from members of the public and advocates in the room and online. You can watch the full recording of this subcommittee here [https://virginiageneralassembly.gov/house/chamber/chamberstream.php] . You can also find the full list of bills the committee is considering here [https://lis.virginia.gov/cgi-bin/legp604.exe?241+sub+H07002] .
How to contact our office
This week my team and I received a plethora of emails covering a wide variety of issues, to include healthcare, the environment and clean energy, gun violence prevention, and small businesses. My team and I sincerely appreciate your thoughtful messages and concerns, as well as your productive ideas for improving our Commonwealth. Make sure to stay in touch throughout the session!
Thank you for reading and following along as we continue our work in Richmond. Please remember to stay in touch to share your ideas! You can contact my office several ways: email us at DelBSewell@house.virginia.gov [DelBSewell@hous.virginia.gov] , call us at 703-261-4787, or visit my Richmond office in person at 201 North 9th St., Suite 905, Richmond, VA 23219.
However you choose to reach out, we look forward to hearing from you and appreciate your continued engagement. I look forward to touching base next week with more updates!
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/NGP/NGP13/1/87444/images/headingcommunitybill%20%281%29.png]

Woodbridge, VA 22195

| | | You're getting this message because you’ve supported good causes and Democratic candidates. We need your support to continue fighting for our democracy. We love having you in our network, but if you no longer wish to hear from us, you can[ unsubscribe here](https://default.salsalabs.org/T600dd5f9-0254-4025-92bc-69e197b8394a/368d17ff-e836-4168-8049-c5f0900fbbf9) _._

| | | | | [](https://default.salsalabs.org/Te4265044-f559-4650-9363-1974abad843d/368d17ff-e836-4168-8049-c5f0900fbbf9) Peter – My name is Harry Dunn and three years ago, I defended the U.S. Capitol and our nation’s leaders against a violent insurrection. _Since that day, I vowed to help ensure that never happens again._ **That’s why I’m officially running for Congress in MD-03 to be the change I want to see for our country and our democracy.[I’d be honored for you to join me and Blue Amp Action in jump starting this campaign by chipping in a split donation of $25 or anything you can:](https://default.salsalabs.org/Tb7661080-edd9-40a3-900e-da53f6ceb01c/368d17ff-e836-4168-8049-c5f0900fbbf9)** [BECOME A FOUNDING DONOR: CHIP IN $25 >>](https://default.salsalabs.org/Tfe61f506-8e7e-41db-b5f8-c6cde3787b08/368d17ff-e836-4168-8049-c5f0900fbbf9) For the last sixteen years, I was a police officer for the United States Capitol where I saw millions of people visit to exercise their rights and lobby their representatives. _And trust me, every political agenda you can think of walked through those doors._ It didn’t matter to me if you were there as a Democrat, Republican, or Independent though, because my job was the same - protect our elected officials and ensure everyone could safely participate in our democracy. But three years ago, under the Capitol Rotunda that took my breath away each day, I was immersed in a profane mix of sweat, screams, shrieks, anger, death, fear, blood, broken limbs, spit, hatred, horror, racism, bigotry, and heroism for what felt like endless hours alongside fellow officers. It was unlike anything we had seen before. Sure, there were heated political moments over the years. But this was different. It was pepper spray, bear spray, and even WD-40 to our faces as we fought back rioters in tactical gear using anything they could as a weapon. It was disorienting chaos as we tried to block every entrance while our elected leaders and capitol staff ran to safety. **It was a direct attack on our democracy.** Many people have tried to deny what happened that day – including some of the same people who stood behind us as we protected them. They’ve diluted the story and muddied the facts to preserve their own political agenda. So I’ve made it a personal mission to share my story, speak truth to power, and work to ensure this never happens again. That’s why a few weeks ago, I retired from the police force, and why I announced my campaign to run for Congress in Maryland’s Third Congressional District. **I’m running because Maryland deserves a Congressman who will put the country above their party, and put the constitution above themselves.[ This will be a competitive race, so I’ve set an ambitious goal to raise $500,000 within the first few weeks of my campaign. Will you chip in to become a Founding Donor and help hit our goal before midnight?](https://default.salsalabs.org/Td2e51fe3-6e14-4c8b-b7b3-26247fb2c4a8/368d17ff-e836-4168-8049-c5f0900fbbf9)**

We love having you in our network, but if you no longer wish to hear from us, you can . | | | | | | | | Peter – My name is Harry Dunn and three years ago, I defended the U.S. Capitol and our nation’s leaders against a violent insurrection. Since that day, I vowed to help ensure that never happens again. That’s why I’m officially running for Congress in MD-03 to be the change I want to see for our country and our democracy. For the last sixteen years, I was a police officer for the United States Capitol where I saw millions of people visit to exercise their rights and lobby their representatives. And trust me, every political agenda you can think of walked through those doors. It didn’t matter to me if you were there as a Democrat, Republican, or Independent though, because my job was the same - protect our elected officials and ensure everyone could safely participate in our democracy. But three years ago, under the Capitol Rotunda that took my breath away each day, I was immersed in a profane mix of sweat, screams, shrieks, anger, death, fear, blood, broken limbs, spit, hatred, horror, racism, bigotry, and heroism for what felt like endless hours alongside fellow officers. It was unlike anything we had seen before. Sure, there were heated political moments over the years. But this was different. It was pepper spray, bear spray, and even WD-40 to our faces as we fought back rioters in tactical gear using anything they could as a weapon. It was disorienting chaos as we tried to block every entrance while our elected leaders and capitol staff ran to safety. It was a direct attack on our democracy. Many people have tried to deny what happened that day – including some of the same people who stood behind us as we protected them. They’ve diluted the story and muddied the facts to preserve their own political agenda. So I’ve made it a personal mission to share my story, speak truth to power, and work to ensure this never happens again. That’s why a few weeks ago, I retired from the police force, and why I announced my campaign to run for Congress in Maryland’s Third Congressional District. body:
So you can imagine the immediate wrath I faced when I went on record supporting Donald J. Trump for President.

| |

---
| | | My fellow Americans - this is Speaker Mike Johnson.

_You've never seen fire and brimstone until you've gone head-to-head with Trump-hating socialists. _

So you can imagine the immediate wrath I faced when I went on record supporting Donald J. Trump for President. I was just talking to my friend, Steve Scalise - he faced the same thing last week when he endorsed Trump too.

_**[He and I agree: as strong Pro-Trump Conservatives, we've got to stick together.](http://e.americanactionnews.com/rd/9z2z442417udref2o2m5hur82b2oijs387ud690rta8_rp22sh2s8i6eo35cdie0o75c1h2bs "He and I agree: as strong Pro-Trump Conservatives, we’ve got to stick together.")**_

That's because the anti-Trump Media... Young radicals on college campuses... the holier-than-thou elites in Hollywood... Democrat Super PACs... Joe Biden's army of megadonors... They are fully committed to destroying our movement and replacing EVERY LAST ONE OF US with a Liberal Democrat.

But wait, that's not even the half of it. It gets worse:
** Problem #1: ** We have THREE imminent Special Elections and Democrats committed more than five million dollars to install more Liberals.

** Problem #2: ** House Democrats have forty million bucks stashed away to attack pro-Trump Conservatives like us.

** Problem #3: ** Joe Biden just bragged about raising a million bucks in a SINGLE DAY attacking President Trump.
I cannot stress the urgency of the situation enough. Early voting is about to start in the first Special Election AND the Left's fundraising advantage grows by the minute...

_**[So as one of my first moves of the election year, I'm teaming up with my fellow Louisianian, Steve Scalise, to set a goal of raising one million dollars between now and the end of the month.](http://e.americanactionnews.com/rd/9z2z08agpu04rq562i0ss7ko24jhhufnh6ff2bj7c50_rp22sh2s8i6eo35cdie0o75c1h2bs "So as one of my first moves of the election year, I’m teaming up with my fellow Louisianian, Steve Scalise, to set a goal of raising one million dollars between now and the end of the month.")**_

I know, I know - that's a big goal. I get that. But that's as low as I could possibly make it to fully fund our campaign operations in every must-win swing state.

If we fail to hit it, the consequences would be unthinkable. We'd have no choice but to: **1) ** SCRAP our get-out-the-vote operations, **2) ** SLASH the budget for our ad campaigns, and **3) ** Throw our digital outreach plans IN THE TRASH CAN.

Nothing - and I mean NOTHING - would be worse for our plans to defend our razor-thin House Majority. **That 's why I'm calling for reinforcements. **

_I know the economy is in bad shape under Joe Biden. So if that 's preventing you from pitching in $100 or $50 - I completely understand. But if you can afford JUST $10 or even $5, I would be grateful beyond measure. _

_**[I only ask everyone reading this to pitch for a few bucks or whatever you can afford.](http://e.americanactionnews.com/rd/9z2z8danu8r7fc65nf348klu59bbhhhj4pj93rkklh8_rp22sh2s8i6eo35cdie0o75c1h2bs "I only ask everyone reading this to pitch for a few bucks or whatever you can afford.")**_

When the stakes are this high, that's what will be the difference between saving our Republican Majority and losing to the Trump-hating Democrats. So can I count on you to pitch in SOMETHING?
---
**[](http://e.americanactionnews.com/rd/9z2z91dkf94k9c1cqij5dtlri1eu39i6nr3falt9g80_rp22sh2s8i6eo35cdie0o75c1h2bs)[**YES >>**](http://e.americanactionnews.com/rd/9z2zcbqe1hlae4gcodavajtpja53mnue5r35tk5gqjo_rp22sh2s8i6eo35cdie0o75c1h2bs)_[**NO >>**](http://e.americanactionnews.com/rd/9z2ze4h5umg6ftnfuh9e33hm36hft4ihn76ep2scph0_rp22sh2s8i6eo35cdie0o75c1h2bs)**
---
Thanks for everything you do.

In liberty,
Mike Johnson (Speaker of the House)

body:
| | | Fellow American, Being a military wife isn’t easy. While my husband Pat was fighting for our country as a Green Beret, I was at home reassuring our daughters that he would come home safe. There were missed holidays, birthdays, and celebrations. There were tears from my children asking where Daddy was. **But I reassured them that their father was doing something bigger than all of us: he was fighting for our country and their future.** Now that Pat’s home for good I’m not going to lie, things have gotten a little easier. It’s amazing seeing what a wonderful husband and father he is every day. **And just because he’s off the battlefield doesn’t mean he’s finished fighting for our daughters’ futures.** **Pat is running for Congress because he believes that America needs more leaders and less politicians. Hi Friend,
Thanks to you, after the New Year I was officially sworn in as a new member of Philadelphia's City Council. It was an incredible to honor and I was thrilled to be surrounded by my family and so many of you in celebration.
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/NGP/NGP59/1/106735/images/back.jpg]
I have gotten right to work and look forward to sharing updates with you on the exciting initiatives that I have in motion to move Philadelphia forward as a healthier city with a stronger future !

I look forward to hearing more from you and ask for your continued partnership in the hard work of improving the lives of every Philadelphian. I know that we can do this together!
Thank you again,
Councilmember Nina Ahmad

---
This is how radical Democrats in Congress are - [**now they want to tear down the Statue of Liberty because Republicans demand we do something about our open southern border.**](https://a1e0.engage.squarespace-mail.com/r?m=65aaca7b0896300ef2c713a9&u=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.clickorlando.com%2Fnews%2Fpolitics%2F2024%2F01%2F19%2Fflorida-lawmaker-proposes-to-remove-statue-of-liberty-over-immigration-bill%2F&w=618846223a022e7ecb41d30c&c=b_65aa950eca574f6b3272c73d&l=en-US&s=Mdugu4HHxpHZBZDzLp4PZZLVNFA%3D)In the last three years, President Biden has done nothing while more than 8 million illegals have walked right into our country.This chart shows how bad it is...
---
|
---
[_ _ Close the Border _ _](https://a1e0.engage.squarespace-mail.com/r?m=65aaca7b0896300ef2c713a9&u=https%3A%2F%2Fsecure.winred.com%2Ftom-barrett-for-congress%2Fsave-liberty&w=618846223a022e7ecb41d30c&c=b_65aa950eca574f6b3272c73d&l=en-US&s=uPlnfveLIY2UluV9b9zGZCgqznA%3D)
---
We are a nation of immigrants, but today, they are coming in unimaginable numbers - **illegally**. Border patrol is overwhelmed, and the fentanyl flowing across our borders is **killing Americans**.It’s time to put a stop to the lawlessness and chaos!
---
[_ _ Save Lady Liberty!_ _](https://a1e0.engage.squarespace-mail.com/r?m=65aaca7b0896300ef2c713a9&u=https%3A%2F%2Fsecure.winred.com%2Ftom-barrett-for-congress%2Fsave-liberty&w=618846223a022e7ecb41d30c&c=b_65aa950eca574f6b3272c73d&l=en-US&s=uPlnfveLIY2UluV9b9zGZCgqznA%3D)
---
I spent 22 years in the U.S. Army defending Lady Liberty and I won’t sit by while radical Democrats tear her down.**I promise you that sealing the border and finishing the wall will be my top priority in Congress.** But I need your help to get there. [**Please send a donation of $10, $25, $50, $100, or $250 today.**](https://a1e0.engage.squarespace-mail.com/r?m=65aaca7b0896300ef2c713a9&u=https%3A%2F%2Fsecure.winred.com%2Ftom-barrett-for-congress%2Fsave-liberty&w=618846223a022e7ecb41d30c&c=b_65aa950eca574f6b3272c73d&l=en-US&s=uPlnfveLIY2UluV9b9zGZCgqznA%3D) Help me raise the funds necessary to defeat Gretchen Whitmer’s hand-picked candidate and put an end to this madness.We can’t afford to wait.

Tom Barrett, U.S. Army (Ret.)Candidate for CongressMichigan’s 7th District

**But first, there are critical elections taking place in PA this year, and we need to start now to ensure voters are registered and ready to make their voices heard.** [**Will you help support our voter registration and engagement campaigns by donating $25 today?**](https://click.everyaction.com/k/77345752/450162949/-1739567893?refcode=EM_F_240119MLK_N_DG_90DO_10_G_B_L1&amount=25&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9BVi9BVjAwMS8xLzkwOTIwIiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogImQyZTM3MjgwLWRkYjYtZWUxMS1iZWExLTAwMjI0ODIyMzdkYSIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=3eJ7FSrij9oJgYabOd2NVsj-yR6-KLDwmHakcb5BO8o=)

My passion for community activism began in Rochester, NY, where I mentored youth and volunteered as a Court Appointed Special Advocate (CASA) for children in foster care. I worked in the disaster services department for the American Red Cross and the Mobile Crisis Team, where I assisted people who were having a mental health crisis.

Now, as a resident of Coatesville, I believe this work to register and engage voters is important because I want my teenage daughter to know that as a _minority woman_ , her voice is important. **And for her to remember that African Americans and women did not always have the right to vote.**

On March 7, 1965, 600 people set out on a 54-mile march from Selma, Alabama, as a peaceful demonstration to secure African American voting rights and to commemorate the death of Jimmie Lee Jackson.

Unfortunately, the demonstrators were met with violence. However, their march was the prelude to the passage of the Voting Rights Act of 1965, which removed voting barriers for Black people across the US.

**This past Monday in Coatesville, in honor of this historic event, we re-enacted the historic Selma March. About 500 marchers showed up, including myself.** **[](https://click.everyaction.com/k/77345753/450162950/-1739567893?refcode=EM_F_240119MLK_N_DG_90DO_10_G_B_P2&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9BVi9BVjAwMS8xLzkwOTIwIiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogImQyZTM3MjgwLWRkYjYtZWUxMS1iZWExLTAwMjI0ODIyMzdkYSIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=3eJ7FSrij9oJgYabOd2NVsj-yR6-KLDwmHakcb5BO8o=)**
It has only been 59 years since Black men and women were granted the ability to vote without facing blatant barriers and discrimination at the ballot box, including literacy tests, poll taxes, and more – **less than one lifetime.**

In 2024, the fight to protect voting rights is ongoing. However, this November, we have the chance to elect legislators who will secure voting rights in PA, end gerrymandering, and more. How? **The _entire_ PA House and half of the State Senate are on the ballot.**

Did you see Mad’s message? We’re up against the first big milestone of 2024 – getting Mad’s name on the ballot. We’ve set a goal to raise $5,000 as we secure the resources and volunteers to get ballot petitions signed.

**[Will you donate $24 today to help us reach that goal?](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/77345811/450163012/-887486310?amount=24&refcode=01192024_MD_MMFR_FR_3&refcode2=cee37280-ddb6-ee11-bea1-0022482237da&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzAvMS85MDQ1OSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJjZWUzNzI4MC1kZGI2LWVlMTEtYmVhMS0wMDIyNDgyMjM3ZGEiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=CtvwndRRVEE8AOMiiJfHO4HPvnqLMr2qVSjyRCkA2ZM=)**

This is our first big test of 2024, and it’s important that we act now to ensure our ballot access program is a success. If you missed Mad’s message, read more below. ↓

— Team Dean **Begin forwarded message:**
> Peter, now that 2024 is officially here, my team and I are getting ready for the first big step of this campaign – getting my name on the ballot.
>
> We call this part of the process the petition period, and my team and I really enjoy it. Despite the cold, it’s a great chance to connect with voters across PA-04 as we collect the 1,000 signatures required to place my name on the ballot.
>
> But in order to get the number of signatures we need on time, we need to make sure we have the resources for collection drives, mailing signature packets to volunteers, and run an intentional volunteer recruitment campaign digitally and on the phones.

| | | Friend – It’s Senator Jacky Rosen, and I'm reaching out because I need your help to defend my Senate seat in Nevada. But first, I want to talk about faith.

My faith has always led me towards working for the betterment of others. As a proud granddaughter of Jewish immigrants and the only former synagogue president in the Senate, I've always been guided by the Jewish principle of Tikkun Olam – **which means to leave the world a better place than how we found it.**

Whether it’s combating climate change, lowering the cost of prescription drugs, or making historic investments in American infrastructure, we've made some crucial steps forward. And each step we've taken is because of your stories, your priorities, and your concerns. But we still have more to do.

**So I'm asking for your help:[Will you split a $5 donation between my campaign and the DSCC, so we can keep fighting for progress in our country and a Democratic Senate majority?](https://go.dscc.org/go/12711?amount=5&t=4&firstname=&lastname=&email=dpwillis67%40gmail.com&addr1=&addr2=&city=Cresco&state=Pennsylvania&zip=18326&phone=None&employer=&occupation=&ask=5&amounts=5%2C10%2C20%2C50&code=DPE-FM-20240119-JackyRosen-DSCCRosenTandem2-ETG-sl1&refcode=DPE-FM-20240119-JackyRosen-DSCCRosenTandem2-ETG-sl1&akid=13265%2E9716520%2Eurz4Kv)**

There's so much at stake in this election. Right now, we're seeing increasing attacks on abortion rights, a sharp rise in antisemitism, and surging right-wing efforts to tear away at the fabric of our democracy itself.

**But even in the face of all the forces amassed against us, I continue to have faith** in the power of individuals like you, to come together and make real, positive change in the world.

We're building a campaign that is powered by everyday people like you who are willing to roll up their sleeves and do the hard, necessary work to make a difference.

**Here at the DLCC, we’re gearing up to face majority-defining special elections in Michigan, New Hampshire, and Pennsylvania.** These elections are not just about winning seats; they're about safeguarding our democracy, and if we want any chance of continuing last year’s winning streak of over _30 special election wins_ , we need your support. 📍**In Pennsylvania,** the House is TIED 101-101. The upcoming special election is _crucial_ to defending Democratic control. Extreme Republicans are itching for payback, so we can’t afford to lose _a single seat._ 📍 **In Michigan** last year, our Democratic trifecta repealed an archaic abortion ban and safeguarded abortion rights. Now, the House is TIED 54-54, and our trifecta is at risk. With _two_ special elections later this year, it’s _imperative_ that we win _both_ specials if we want to protect our majority. 📍 **In New Hampshire,** the Republican majority is as thin as it gets. We’re only four seats away from FLIPPING the House, making right now the perfect opportunity to tip the scales in our favor. And your $7 donation could be the deciding factor in whether our Dems _win_ or _lose._ **These races will set the tone for our upcoming elections this year. # **A Message from the Chairwoman**
---
| | ** _Tentative Schedule for 2024 Congress of Counties Released_**
---
Friends, We are just over a month away from our 2024 Congress of Counties on February 23-24 at Crowne Plaza Union Station in Downtown Indianapolis. We are excited to let you know that the tentative schedule for the weekend has been posted on our [Congress of Counties website](http://ci.criticalimpact.com/go/1/f7f15e9875c39250df60ac364a9f256a/40313/7838b714a021b4983947229f28c3afba/23e509e1d64740b2c3d6b838967d376c/40313). This is an amazing opportunity to come together as grassroots leaders and share in fellowship and fun as we discuss the best ways to support our county organizations and our campaigns. Whether you have come to every Congress of Counties, or have never been before, we have something for everyone. Our goal is to provide educational opportunities so that grassroots leaders can take what they learn back to their communities to strengthen their local county GOPs, to help win elections, and continue to build a better Indiana. And most importantly, we plan to have a lot of fun! This event is filling up fast, so don't wait! Please be sure to [sign up ASAP](http://ci.criticalimpact.com/go/1/f7f15e9875c39250df60ac364a9f256a/40313/7838b714a021b4983947229f28c3afba/a5c6887d3a92e836c3d6b838967d376c/40313) to reserve your spot at the 2024 Congress of Counties. We are looking forward to seeing you and working with you. Thank you for all that you do.
---
---
Chairwoman Anne F. Hathaway

# _Gov. Holcomb Announced a New Workforce Development Campaign_
---
---
| | [](http://ci.criticalimpact.com/go/1/f7f15e9875c39250df60ac364a9f256a/40313/7838b714a021b4983947229f28c3afba/4eb13eee8f246df3c3d6b838967d376c/40313)**Governor Eric Holcomb** , [announced](http://ci.criticalimpact.com/go/1/f7f15e9875c39250df60ac364a9f256a/40313/7838b714a021b4983947229f28c3afba/0198333546385b3bc3d6b838967d376c/40313) “One Stop to Start” a workforce development campaign designed to raise awareness and help connect Hoosiers with existing workforce and job-related training programs and resources. The One Stop to Start website is [live now!](http://ci.criticalimpact.com/go/1/f7f15e9875c39250df60ac364a9f256a/40313/7838b714a021b4983947229f28c3afba/f398890614e0408bc3d6b838967d376c/40313) **What he’s saying** : “The overall goal of ‘One Stop to Start’ is to make sure that Hoosiers have awareness of and access to the programs that can get them on that path to realizing a high-wage career, ...Perhaps it’s a short-term certificate or a two- or four-year degree. There’s a pathway for all Hoosiers, and ‘One Stop to Start’ will help individuals discover various options that fit their needs”, **Gov. Holcomb** said in a [press release](http://ci.criticalimpact.com/go/1/f7f15e9875c39250df60ac364a9f256a/40313/7838b714a021b4983947229f28c3afba/cfcc90df21357f61c3d6b838967d376c/40313).
**What else happened this week? Gov. Holcomb[](http://ci.criticalimpact.com/go/1/f7f15e9875c39250df60ac364a9f256a/40313/7838b714a021b4983947229f28c3afba/00812557e320fbe2c3d6b838967d376c/40313)[](http://ci.criticalimpact.com/go/1/f7f15e9875c39250df60ac364a9f256a/40313/7838b714a021b4983947229f28c3afba/75bca1a2bef5cc0ec3d6b838967d376c/40313)** [joined](http://ci.criticalimpact.com/go/1/f7f15e9875c39250df60ac364a9f256a/40313/7838b714a021b4983947229f28c3afba/5e4ccdd97b3ae321c3d6b838967d376c/40313) the Indiana Civil Rights Commission in celebrating Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. At the Statehouse.

Holcomb** on [Facebook](http://ci.criticalimpact.com/go/1/f7f15e9875c39250df60ac364a9f256a/40313/7838b714a021b4983947229f28c3afba/0ceb391837a5a8fdc3d6b838967d376c/40313) or [Twitter](http://ci.criticalimpact.com/go/1/f7f15e9875c39250df60ac364a9f256a/40313/7838b714a021b4983947229f28c3afba/740e47893a41838ec3d6b838967d376c/40313).

# 💰📈Record Breaking 2023 for the IEDC! What is CapEx?

---
---
| | CapEx refers to capital expenditures made by companies to take on new projects or expansions. The Indiana Economic Development Corporation has [reported](http://ci.criticalimpact.com/go/1/f7f15e9875c39250df60ac364a9f256a/40313/7838b714a021b4983947229f28c3afba/a2c9ba67fe28cc62c3d6b838967d376c/40313) 7 straight years of record setting CapEx, and in 2023 those numbers reached new heights!
---
| | The IEDC is charged with growing the state economy, driving economic development, and helping businesses launch, grow, and locate in the state. A high CapEx means a couple of things: 1) Businesses recognize Indiana as the #1 state to start a business and they have invested in Hoosiers. 2) Republican leaders have created a great environment for growth and expansion, so current Indiana entrepreneurs have been able to invest in new projects. What does this mean for Hoosiers? It means more jobs coming to the state, higher paying jobs coming to the state, and economic stability. What else does this mean for Hoosiers, beyond high paying jobs and a stable economy? It means advancements for infrastructure, stronger small businesses, and opportunities for Hoosier entrepreneurs. A strong economy is good for all Hoosiers. A rising tide lifts all boats!

**ICYMI: MD Sheriff's Join John Teichert For Law Enforcement Coalition Announcement**
**BALTIMORE, Md.** – Brigadier General (ret) John Teichert rolled out his latest coalition in Westminster on Thursday afternoon with several of Maryland’s finest showing their support as part of the group.
[](https://teichertformaryland.us13.list-manage.com/track/click?u=1ec0c6fa331e836475672e631&id=a2a08e6bea&e=1b1fb1ad9f)
Flanked by Sheriff Joe Gamble of Talbot county and Sheriff Matthew Crisafulli of Worcester county, Teichert shared his vision to support our law enforcement officials and clean up our streets as crime rages on.
**“Unfortunately here in Maryland, and in many places around our country, our politicians, including my opponents, are saying just the opposite of that,”** Teichert said during today’s press conference. **“They're saying to law enforcement, we don't trust you, we don't appreciate you and we won't fully support you. And as a result, we see these pro criminal policies that ultimately degrade law and order in our communities and ignore the needs of the community and law abiding citizens.”**
Sheriff Gamble expressed his support for the kind of leadership Teichert could bring to Washington, stating in part, **“There’s just a total lack of leadership. He supports law enforcement. He understands our issues. We've talked a great length about those issues, the support for law enforcement, but more importantly, the support for public safety because that's what we represent.”**
Meanwhile, Sheriff Crisafulli noted there’s also the issue of the juvenile reform act, where children under 13 are not criminally responsible for their actions. **“There is that caveat of children 10 to 12 that can be charged only with a crime of violence, and or a firearm related offense and what that has done to communities throughout this state. It has increased the juvenile crime rate, it has emboldened juveniles. and we need leadership like General John Teichert, at the United States level to get in and to get behind law enforcement officers. And as both gentlemen have indicated and get behind their families because their families also sacrifice, when their husbands and wives are out here on the front lines.”**
As Teichert seeks to clean up our crime-ridden streets as our next U.S. Senator in Maryland, he does so with the support of the men and women in blue. The law enforcement coalition is the second coalition launch of his campaign following the veterans coalition.
See the first round of coalition members below:
* Sheriff Joe Gamble, Talbot County
* Sheriff Mike Lewis, Wicomico County
* Sheriff Matthew Crisafulli, Worcester County
* Sheriff James Phillips Jr., Dorchester County

I want to thank you for all the support you’ve given me over the last week, and I can’t wait to finally turn my attention back to the issues that Michiganders actually care about. I’m going to be spending the next few days traveling across Michigan and speaking to voters about the importance of abortion rights in the 2024 Election — but before I tell you more about it, = | = This upcoming Monday will mark the 51st anniversary of the Supreme Court ruling in favor of Roe v. Wade. I wish that we could spend time celebrating the fact that women and girls have the ability to exercise their reproductive rights regardless of where they live. But unfortunately, we have to confront a harsh reality. The decades-long assault on reproductive freedom by extremist Republicans has allowed far-right politicians to pass laws restricting and even banning abortion in statehouses all across the country. I’m very proud of the fact that not a day has gone by where women and girls in Michigan couldn’t access reproductive rights — but that could be in jeopardy if MAGA extremists win in 2024 and fulfill their promise of banning abortion nationwide. I’ll be spending the next few days traveling around Michigan to make sure that Michiganders know how important the upcoming election is for the future of abortion rights. Look, big change starts small.
That's a lesson that my grandmother, Polly Noonan, first taught me decades ago. Well before most women had any political power, my grandmother organized women into a political force in Albany.
By the time I was in elementary school, I was tagging along with her to all kinds of Democratic campaign headquarters, rallies and events. She remains one of my biggest role models — and I carry her wisdom with me to this day. **She taught me that my voice matters, that women’s voices matter and that grassroots activism matters. And she showed me how campaigns are won by the people who put in the work like the volunteers knocking doors, stuffing envelopes, turning out the vote and donating what they can, when they can.**
For decades, first by my grandmother's side and then as a public servant myself, I've seen how those small grassroots actions all add up to victory on Election Day. That's how Democrats defeated the odds in 2022 to defend and even expand our Senate majority. And that's why I know that we can win again in 2024.
With Democrats defending 23 seats, the odds are certainly stacked against us. And after the 2022 red wave in New York, Republicans here are already targeting my seat for defeat. **But when people like you get off the sidelines and chip in even just $3, eventually we'll build a grassroots movement capable of defeating even the GOP's wealthiest megadonors.**
**[So please, will you chip in $3 or $25 or whatever you can spare today to help save our Senate majority by building a grassroots movement one grassroots gift at a time? Friend,

Since the moment I got off the stage, I wanted to let you know how grateful I am for your support. Generosity from grassroots supporters like you is the reason I am able to fund my campaign and fight for America's future.

Now, I want to take a few minutes to talk with you about the journey I have been on. **[Once you've finished reading this, please consider making a contribution of any amount to help me fund my campaign so I can get my message out to every voter!](http://links.reclamingamericanfreedom.com/u/click?_t=5ec072595b1347f09b4bac0de82ea87d&_m=1e813ab490874ce2a1a599df55c5fb20&_e=WfeqQwcygcP6LJ4zb6eC5bu_XoKxb7GCNTwSA-4mX7-G10n8C5rjxjnOxuiGHDpRfXBrh4T0DRRaHquYl8XiY7v_jAfpdI3B1Bej60yZhKOu9L9JyMhWahYh5r5QtzatUk_vjsYEXfdb4-UPo-LusFirlyQBi7Zwk2izlbL_kFTCHdRylT8k-oJ-ZOEp9i8xjvLQGBoRJGAJlHsIhv90O-jRzhgFzZK811h9R4Sjo_6RS6dxOwXx4CHGUvabrXLzirntbRQzSnNP9VRu7Ry12yWSxhXtj1FMwlrRMrfA6ukEDlwIBUDM7Ck8w_un1_ZnRBPHKds4rVji4E6dBbJZEpuWxrqnXD7r8yAu0gvTZg-yK2BadLnVIkAgDtyXo78pEnOHP_wNCIHhI5_Ie0j3ZOIiZG8FQdC4UejRdtTO7ccjNhLu6RhfUUnp7x2VgpwYwl0yWF5rSZ3KYi_E9rE0pX3gBkWjtqZr_AGMpjWgVZpU-3PAGU_L69Jd_2Z59kSnD54vSzjAKTJb0OUb2cvI-rIkLuR3ijgNj8oruxARGvgZBD7SkCkRtnUknVZfluGPRoxcBJGSRW19QFgI14LtFBUjHpEG0qnrh4iG7HlK_WiijWPHiVLyXBDDGNiII7w4 "Once you’ve finished reading this, please consider making a contribution of any amount to help me fund my campaign so I can get my message out to every voter!")**

Ever since I launched my campaign for President, I have read and heard my life described in every way imaginable. _**Today, I want you to hear my story in MY words.**_
---
| | | | [](http://links.reclamingamericanfreedom.com/u/click?_t=5ec072595b1347f09b4bac0de82ea87d&_m=1e813ab490874ce2a1a599df55c5fb20&_e=WfeqQwcygcP6LJ4zb6eC5bu_XoKxb7GCNTwSA-4mX7-G10n8C5rjxjnOxuiGHDpRfXBrh4T0DRRaHquYl8XiY7v_jAfpdI3B1Bej60yZhKOu9L9JyMhWahYh5r5QtzatUk_vjsYEXfdb4-UPo-LusFirlyQBi7Zwk2izlbL_kFTCHdRylT8k-oJ-ZOEp9i8xjvLQGBoRJGAJlHsIhv90O-jRzhgFzZK811h9R4Sjo_6RS6dxOwXx4CHGUvabrXLzirntbRQzSnNP9VRu7Ry12yWSxhXtj1FMwlrRMrfA6ukEDlwIBUDM7Ck8w_un1_ZnRBPHKds4rVji4E6dBbJZEpuWxrqnXD7r8yAu0gvTZg-yK2BadLnVIkAgDtyXo78pEnOHP_wNCIHhI5_Ie0j3ZOIiZG8FQdC4UejRdtTO7ccjNhLu6RhfUUnp7x2VgpwYwl0yWF5rSZ3KYi_E9rE0pX3gBkWjtqZr_AGMpjWgVZoRMJeEfg9Gn3NrsnAgk7KNWMICDVlVUq-1I8VX6gxEA-vObmgJmU3J4GTvs_MJqkoVMjCCH8mzmixtgWtgeb643nF_s4e8QGdxbCbf0J7h59V9iTNjeWbTe-uhX7Sv-uZbrPfLyEa77Q0uXOhmxou0)
---
| I am the daughter of legal immigrants from a small, rural town in South Carolina. We were the only Indian family in our town. My father wore a turban as he still does to this day, and my mother wore a sari. No one knew who we were, what we were, or why we were there. But with each passing day, the community began to look beyond our skin color. They began to see my family for who we are: hard working people who held the same values they cherished. Gradually, those initial stares transformed into smiles and we shifted from being excluded to embraced. Not every day was perfect. But every day was better than the one before it.
---
After graduating from Clemson and working in the corporate world, I decided to take a job working for my family's business that my mother started in our living room when I was a child. I was frustrated when I saw how hard it was to make a dollar and how easy it was for government to take it away. When I voiced these frustrations to my mom, she gave me some wise advice which was: _" Don't complain. Do something about it." _
---
| | | So, that's exactly what I did and I decided to run for state legislature. But it wasn't easy. I ran against the longest-serving legislator in the state and hardly anyone thought I had a chance. I was polling at 15 percent a week before the primary. **But the people of South Carolina took a chance on me, and we won. ➡️**
---
| | [](http://links.reclamingamericanfreedom.com/u/click?_t=5ec072595b1347f09b4bac0de82ea87d&_m=1e813ab490874ce2a1a599df55c5fb20&_e=WfeqQwcygcP6LJ4zb6eC5bu_XoKxb7GCNTwSA-4mX7-G10n8C5rjxjnOxuiGHDpRfXBrh4T0DRRaHquYl8XiY7v_jAfpdI3B1Bej60yZhKOu9L9JyMhWahYh5r5QtzatUk_vjsYEXfdb4-UPo-LusFirlyQBi7Zwk2izlbL_kFTCHdRylT8k-oJ-ZOEp9i8xjvLQGBoRJGAJlHsIhv90O-jRzhgFzZK811h9R4Sjo_6RS6dxOwXx4CHGUvabrXLzirntbRQzSnNP9VRu7Ry12yWSxhXtj1FMwlrRMrfA6ukEDlwIBUDM7Ck8w_un1_ZnRBPHKds4rVji4E6dBbJZEpuWxrqnXD7r8yAu0gvTZg-yK2BadLnVIkAgDtyXo78pEnOHP_wNCIHhI5_Ie0j3ZOIiZG8FQdC4UejRdtTO7ccjNhLu6RhfUUnp7x2VgpwYwl0yWF5rSZ3KYi_E9rE0pX3gBkWjtqZr_AGMpjWgVZr1ZWXnESLiHcLO7vp4PaAwYgpJpKTrzaDQZNt1y0RhkxLYMRa9oPVUTxPtILoh9O2V9auzl6_vQOUnJuFyEBSwdpgUoNQTPMEAdQZGz4ZzgliCymPVBOl31dCxjvCcqSBSS3ClNYeoft3LO50mMAzE)
---
It was an honor to serve the people as a state legislator. I fought against the status quo and stood up for the people of my district. When I fought for government transparency by pushing to make sure important votes were on the record, my colleagues retaliated. They stripped me of my committees. So I decided to run for governor.

When I campaigned for governor, people didn't know who I was. I was polling in fourth place, with limited time until Election Day. I was the least funded and least known GOP candidate. But together, we defied expectations and won. Then, we made a difference in South Carolina by cutting taxes, creating thousands of jobs, and revitalizing our economy.

When I was nominated as Ambassador to the United Nations, people said I didn't have the experience. I proved them wrong. When I got to the UN, I took the "kick me" sign off our back. I told the world that America would have the backs of our allies, and for those who did not have our backs, we were taking names! The dictators, murderers, and thieves at the UN didn't know what hit them.

---
| [](http://links.reclamingamericanfreedom.com/u/click?_t=5ec072595b1347f09b4bac0de82ea87d&_m=1e813ab490874ce2a1a599df55c5fb20&_e=WfeqQwcygcP6LJ4zb6eC5bu_XoKxb7GCNTwSA-4mX7-G10n8C5rjxjnOxuiGHDpRfXBrh4T0DRRaHquYl8XiY7v_jAfpdI3B1Bej60yZhKOu9L9JyMhWahYh5r5QtzatUk_vjsYEXfdb4-UPo-LusFirlyQBi7Zwk2izlbL_kFTCHdRylT8k-oJ-ZOEp9i8xjvLQGBoRJGAJlHsIhv90O-jRzhgFzZK811h9R4Sjo_6RS6dxOwXx4CHGUvabrXLzirntbRQzSnNP9VRu7Ry12yWSxhXtj1FMwlrRMrfA6ukEDlwIBUDM7Ck8w_un1_ZnRBPHKds4rVji4E6dBbJZEpuWxrqnXD7r8yAu0gvTZg-yK2BadLnVIkAgDtyXo78pEnOHP_wNCIHhI5_Ie0j3ZOIiZG8FQdC4UejRdtTO7ccjNhLu6RhfUUnp7x2VgpwYwl0yWF5rSZ3KYi_E9rE0pX3gBkWjtqZr_AGMpjWgVZpQ4vntSbvr6gU4c76sbgkdoDe-bTIFND-Ycduj0m8CrGPgI26xX5tsFNVcAVGPqJC-dApib0bY4-7iKwYQ5bQ2r0hIt9DwqOymXSqCnpBF5XSnMN2iy5b1j7aqBE7ZMGIQbpBndpmLUjtPORJ1jNVG)

My name is Nikki Haley. I want to tell you a bit about myself and why I'm running for President of the United States.

I'm running for President because my parents came to America more than 50 years ago - an America that was strong and proud, and full of opportunities. I want them to know that America again.

I'm running for President as a military spouse. My husband is deployed and I want him and his military brothers and sisters to know their sacrifice means something - that we do love this country.

I'm running for President for the future of our kids. I have a daughter who just got married and I saw how hard it was for her and her husband to buy a home. I'm doing this for my son who's a senior in college and shouldn't have to worry about saying things on a paper that he doesn't believe in just to get an A.

I'm running for my daughter, my son, and our future generations. I want them to experience the freedom and opportunity that the American Dream has to offer.

_**I 'm running for President because we have a country to save! **_

I've seen that even on our worst days, we are blessed to live in America. But I also know that under Biden's leadership, times are tough, our future is slipping, and America can be doing so much better.

**As governor, I was dubbed a "jobs governor"** because I slashed our unemployment rate, brought jobs back to our state, and shepherded in a successful economic recovery.

**At the UN I fought for America,** made sure our allies knew we had their backs and stood up to murderers and dictators to let them know that America was taking names.

I know how to make America strong and proud because I've done it before. **And I 'll do it as your next President. **

As President, I'll revitalize our economy, support small businesses, stop Washington's spending sprees, protect our border, champion school choice, and save America's future.

clean_body: I wanted to let you know how grateful I am for your support. | | | | | | Friend, Since the moment I got off the stage, I wanted to let you know how grateful I am for your support. Generosity from grassroots supporters like you is the reason I am able to fund my campaign and fight for America's future. Now, I want to take a few minutes to talk with you about the journey I have been on. "Once you’ve finished reading this, please consider making a contribution of any amount to help me fund my campaign so I can get my message out to every voter!" Ever since I launched my campaign for President, I have read and heard my life described in every way imaginable. Today, I want you to hear my story in MY words. | | | | | I am the daughter of legal immigrants from a small, rural town in South Carolina. We were the only Indian family in our town. My father wore a turban as he still does to this day, and my mother wore a sari. No one knew who we were, what we were, or why we were there. But with each passing day, the community began to look beyond our skin color. They began to see my family for who we are: hard working people who held the same values they cherished. Gradually, those initial stares transformed into smiles and we shifted from being excluded to embraced. Not every day was perfect. But every day was better than the one before it. After graduating from Clemson and working in the corporate world, I decided to take a job working for my family's business that my mother started in our living room when I was a child. I was frustrated when I saw how hard it was to make a dollar and how easy it was for government to take it away. When I voiced these frustrations to my mom, she gave me some wise advice which was: " Don't complain. Do something about it." | | | So, that's exactly what I did and I decided to run for state legislature. But it wasn't easy. I ran against the longest-serving legislator in the state and hardly anyone thought I had a chance. I was polling at 15 percent a week before the primary. But the people of South Carolina took a chance on me, and we won. ➡️ | | It was an honor to serve the people as a state legislator. I fought against the status quo and stood up for the people of my district. When I fought for government transparency by pushing to make sure important votes were on the record, my colleagues retaliated. They stripped me of my committees. So I decided to run for governor. When I campaigned for governor, people didn't know who I was. I was polling in fourth place, with limited time until Election Day. I was the least funded and least known GOP candidate. But together, we defied expectations and won. Then, we made a difference in South Carolina by cutting taxes, creating thousands of jobs, and revitalizing our economy. When I was nominated as Ambassador to the United Nations, people said I didn't have the experience. I proved them wrong. When I got to the UN, I took the "kick me" sign off our back. I told the world that America would have the backs of our allies, and for those who did not have our backs, we were taking names! The dictators, murderers, and thieves at the UN didn't know what hit them. | Now, I'm running for President because our country is heading down a path of doubt, division, and self-destruction. We need a leader who will rise to the occasion, offer solutions, and prioritize serving the people over the political class. "It would mean a lot to me if every single person reading this today could send a donation of just $5 to help me keep my campaign momentum STRONG! >>" Your donation will not only show that my campaign is a force to be reckoned with, but it will also play a vital role in helping fund our campaign in the upcoming days. "Will you consider making a one-time donation of any amount today to show the strength of OUR movement?" | | Friend, throughout my life, I've been shaking up the status quo. I'm hoping to do the same as your next President. But in order to get there, "I need your help – starting right now. " Your contribution is what keeps this movement alive and thriving, so thank you for standing with me. My very best, | Nikki Haley | | | | | | | | "NikkiHaleyMerch" | | "Claim Your Mug" | | More About Nikki Haley | "NikkiHaleyPodium" My name is Nikki Haley. I want to tell you a bit about myself and why I'm running for President of the United States. I'm running for President because my parents came to America more than 50 years ago - an America that was strong and proud, and full of opportunities. I want them to know that America again. I'm running for President as a military spouse. My husband is deployed and I want him and his military brothers and sisters to know their sacrifice means something - that we do love this country. I'm running for President for the future of our kids. I have a daughter who just got married and I saw how hard it was for her and her husband to buy a home. I'm doing this for my son who's a senior in college and shouldn't have to worry about saying things on a paper that he doesn't believe in just to get an A. I'm running for my daughter, my son, and our future generations. I want them to experience the freedom and opportunity that the American Dream has to offer. I 'm running for President because we have a country to save! I've seen that even on our worst days, we are blessed to live in America. But I also know that under Biden's leadership, times are tough, our future is slipping, and America can be doing so much better. As governor, I was dubbed a "jobs governor" because I slashed our unemployment rate, brought jobs back to our state, and shepherded in a successful economic recovery. At the UN I fought for America, made sure our allies knew we had their backs and stood up to murderers and dictators to let them know that America was taking names. I know how to make America strong and proud because I've done it before. And I 'll do it as your next President. After earning his undergraduate degree, Ron DeSantis graduated from Harvard Law School, but was so moved by the events of September 11, 2001, that he volunteered to serve in the Navy to fight for our freedom. When he returned, he started a life of public service by serving Florida as both Congressman and now Governor. Despite all his years of fighting to ensure the American people enjoy the freedom we're promised in this country, he's watched the Left strip away freedoms at every turn and impose radical agendas on children, families, and consumers nationwide. In 2009, Ron met the love of his life Casey in Florida, and he's now the proud father of 6, 5, and 3-year-old children. Friend,
Wouldn't you know it? Another GOP grifter seeking elected office in Ohio--and receiving Trump's endorsement, of course--has a record of shady business dealings running a car dealership.
The AP reported that Bernie Moreno, a Trump-backed candidate trying to unseat U.S. Senator Sherrod Brown, faced multiple discrimination lawsuits related to his Cleveland car dealership. Peter,

and insurance mogul Alex Dubitsky is inviting friends to pay up to $6,600

primary.

Thanks for anything you can give to fuel our work to re-elect Jamaal this

Geoff Simpson

| There is a heated debate in Congress right now over border security legislation being drafted in the Senate.
We don't know exactly what is in the deal, but this is what I'm looking for:

* Ceasing the mass parole - i.e. catch and release - of illegal immigrants that the Biden Administration has allowed.

* Reforms to our asylum laws to close the loopholes that incentivize primarily economic migrants to claim asylum to gain entry into our country.

* Reimplementation of programs like the Remain in Mexico policy that prevents migrants from being released into the interior of our country while their asylum claim is adjudicated.

These are the major policy changes that need to be in this package for me to take this seriously and consider voting for it. But I'm not going to reflexively oppose this legislation without seeing it.
There are some in our party who are more interested in sound bites than policy making. Some are making the argument that we should shut the government down if we don't get border security. And there are some who argue we should wait until 2025, when there may be a Republican in the White House, to consider any legislation.
Both arguments are nonsensical. If we shut the government down, we will lose that political battle, have the blame for the shutdown be placed squarely at our feet, and never have the opportunity to implement border security measures. Our leverage is Ukraine aid, which the White House wants and which we need to deny unless we have serious policy changes at the southern border.
And we cannot wait another year to address the unprecedented crisis at our southern border. As a Texan, I will not sit by while my state continues to bear the brunt of illegal immigration because there are those who would rather play politics with this issue.
My only priority is border security. And we must do everything to achieve it.

| In the aftermath of the overturning of Roe v. Wade, many might ask why this march is still important. Here's why we still march:
1\. We march because the Biden Administration is actively trying to defund pregnancy centers. It should not be controversial to provide care and resources so that mothers choose life.
For a group of people who claim to be pro-choice, progressives are revealing that they're actually just pro-abortion.
2\. We march because the Biden Administration has politicized the FDA, and is working to roll back major safety protocols that limit chemical abortion.
As with all abortion, chemical abortion is bad for women. In fact, there is a 53% greater risk of ER visits for chemical abortion as opposed to surgical abortion. That's from analyzing insurance claims data.
3\. We march because Democrats support abortion until the point of birth.
This is completely out of step with the majority of Americans. Not only are we on the moral side of the argument, 69% of Americans support some limits on abortion. We have an obligation to not compromise our morals and keep fighting until abortion is a terrible relic of human history.
That is why the March for Life is still so vitally important.

| There's a strange new trend with some people on our side who have recently decided that Ronald Reagan is "not conservative" enough, and a relic of the past. They're wrong.
There is still so much we can learn from Reagan's conservative legacy, relevant to important fights happening in America today.
The key thing to understand about Reaganism is that Reagan did not fight just to fight. Reagan fought to win on critical fronts in the culture wars.
As we look at fighting the DEI ideology that is destroying higher education right now, we should look to Reagan's higher education battles.
What did Reagan do when University of California administrators coddled student and faculty radicals that were rioting? He sent in the National Guard. What did he do when the violence continued? He shut down all 28 public colleges and universities in the state for four days. Not to mention, he also did the serious work of instituting budgetary reforms to prevent the administrative bloat that we see in higher education today.
We have to take the same approach. That means confronting the taxpayer-funded DEI that has propped up left-wing illiberalism and enabled the explosion of antisemitism we see on college campuses. How do we do this? Let's start by creating smart higher ed policy.
I have a bill that will prevent taxpayer dollars from flowing to universities that force students to write DEI statements. Most Americans know the left is crazy, but we have to make sure that conservatives look like the adults in the room.
It's important to acknowledge Reagan's conservative legacy, learn lessons from him, and implement those lessons in our political debates today.

clean_body: | | | | | | | | == | Peter – This week, I outlined the urgent need for Congress to act on border security. I also outlined the reason behind the March for Life, which took place this week in our nation's capital, and defended Ronald Reagan's conservative legacy in the face of misplaced criticism from our own side. As always, the support of committed patriots like you is the lifeblood of my campaign. I'm choosing to run for re-election because I believe our country is still worth fighting for, and because I want to continue the progress we've made for the conservative movement and sound conservative policies over the past 5 years. If you're willing to contribute anything at all to my campaign, I would greatly appreciate it as my primary election quickly approaches. | | | == | As always, thank you for your continued support. Now, here's your brief. | | | | | | | | MY PRIORITY IS BORDER SECURITY | | | | == | There is a heated debate in Congress right now over border security legislation being drafted in the Senate. We don't know exactly what is in the deal, but this is what I'm looking for: Ceasing the mass parole - i.e. catch and release - of illegal immigrants that the Biden Administration has allowed. Reforms to our asylum laws to close the loopholes that incentivize primarily economic migrants to claim asylum to gain entry into our country. * Reimplementation of programs like the Remain in Mexico policy that prevents migrants from being released into the interior of our country while their asylum claim is adjudicated. These are the major policy changes that need to be in this package for me to take this seriously and consider voting for it. But I'm not going to reflexively oppose this legislation without seeing it. There are some in our party who are more interested in sound bites than policy making. Some are making the argument that we should shut the government down if we don't get border security. And there are some who argue we should wait until 2025, when there may be a Republican in the White House, to consider any legislation. Both arguments are nonsensical. If we shut the government down, we will lose that political battle, have the blame for the shutdown be placed squarely at our feet, and never have the opportunity to implement border security measures. Our leverage is Ukraine aid, which the White House wants and which we need to deny unless we have serious policy changes at the southern border. And we cannot wait another year to address the unprecedented crisis at our southern border. As a Texan, I will not sit by while my state continues to bear the brunt of illegal immigration because there are those who would rather play politics with this issue. My only priority is border security. And we must do everything to achieve it. | | | | | | | | WHY WE MARCH | | In the aftermath of the overturning of Roe v. Wade, many might ask why this march is still important. Here's why we still march: 1\. We march because the Biden Administration is actively trying to defund pregnancy centers. It should not be controversial to provide care and resources so that mothers choose life. For a group of people who claim to be pro-choice, progressives are revealing that they're actually just pro-abortion. 2\. We march because the Biden Administration has politicized the FDA, and is working to roll back major safety protocols that limit chemical abortion. As with all abortion, chemical abortion is bad for women. In fact, there is a 53% greater risk of ER visits for chemical abortion as opposed to surgical abortion. That's from analyzing insurance claims data. 3\. We march because Democrats support abortion until the point of birth. This is completely out of step with the majority of Americans. Not only are we on the moral side of the argument, 69% of Americans support some limits on abortion. We have an obligation to not compromise our morals and keep fighting until abortion is a terrible relic of human history. That is why the March for Life is still so vitally important. | | | | | | REAGAN'S CONSERVATIVE LEGACY | | == | There's a strange new trend with some people on our side who have recently decided that Ronald Reagan is "not conservative" enough, and a relic of the past. They're wrong. There is still so much we can learn from Reagan's conservative legacy, relevant to important fights happening in America today. The key thing to understand about Reaganism is that Reagan did not fight just to fight. Reagan fought to win on critical fronts in the culture wars. As we look at fighting the DEI ideology that is destroying higher education right now, we should look to Reagan's higher education battles. What did Reagan do when University of California administrators coddled student and faculty radicals that were rioting? He sent in the National Guard. What did he do when the violence continued? He shut down all 28 public colleges and universities in the state for four days. Not to mention, he also did the serious work of instituting budgetary reforms to prevent the administrative bloat that we see in higher education today. We have to take the same approach. That means confronting the taxpayer-funded DEI that has propped up left-wing illiberalism and enabled the explosion of antisemitism we see on college campuses. How do we do this? Let's start by creating smart higher ed policy. I have a bill that will prevent taxpayer dollars from flowing to universities that force students to write DEI statements. Most Americans know the left is crazy, but we have to make sure that conservatives look like the adults in the room. It's important to acknowledge Reagan's conservative legacy, learn lessons from him, and implement those lessons in our political debates today. | | | | | | | | == | | | == | My custom eyepatch is back in stock - with options for left or right eye. | Hey there.

This is an existential fight. **And that can feel heavy.**

We’re up against massive fossil fuel giants with deep pockets and an army of political lobbyists at their beck and call. Even though I’ve been at this as long as I have, there are days when I wonder if we're even making a dent. **But we can’t give up.**

Not now, not ever. The work we’re doing here is more critical now than ever. Together, we’re advancing policies that tackle the climate crisis at its roots — the fossil fuel industry. At the same time, we’re electing climate champions up and down the ballot, and calling out elected officials who prioritize short-term profit over a livable future for all of our communities.

None of us can do this work alone, and I’m honored to consider you a partner in this work. So, I want to hear from you. On those tough days, how do you stay motivated for climate justice? Is it thinking about the next generation? The strength and resilience of our community? Perhaps a personal experience that made you think differently? I’ve had my share of wake-up calls and moments that kept me going.

I want to hear yours.

**_[Your stories not only inspire me, but they’re what keeps our movement powerful. There is no right or wrong answer. body:
We grew up on stories of service from our parents and grandparents. Their legacy inspired our own service.
#
Derek:
We grew up on stories of service from our parents and grandparents. Their legacy inspired our own service.
The Greatest Generation fought dictators, fascists, and authoritarians — people who brought the world to the brink. For the benefit of the entire world, they were defeated.
Our generation has a fight of our own. We aren’t going to raise the American flag over Iwo Jima, or punch a Nazi in the face at Omaha Beach. But we will fight.
Our challenge is to stop the rise of dictators, fascists, and authoritarians here at home.
Make no mistake: Trump and his supporters are fashioning themselves after the same people that our parents and grandparents fought. Absolute control.
If we defeat them, we can save our democracy. If we fail, we could fall into darkness.
Those are the stakes. And VoteVets will be in this fight every minute until Election Day. Are you with us?

Not only do the millions of illegal immigrants who are entering our country know that the border is WIDE OPEN thanks to the Democrat in the White House. My district is one of the best chances to chip away at the iron grip these radicals have in the Golden State. body:
I wanted to let you know how grateful I am for your support.
188d92cdddd40f90da47bc74ea2ba8fb
| |
---
| | | | [](http://post.spmailtechnol.com/f/a/JaiCnWsj_9Bbw3Attqdp9w~~/AARclAA~/RgRnjVB-~)
---

Friend,

Since the moment I got off the stage, I wanted to let you know how grateful I am for your support. Generosity from grassroots supporters like you is the reason I am able to fund my campaign and fight for America's future.

Now, I want to take a few minutes to talk with you about the journey I have been on. **[Once you've finished reading this, please consider making a contribution of any amount to help me fund my campaign so I can get my message out to every voter!](http://post.spmailtechnol.com/f/a/JaiCnWsj_9Bbw3Attqdp9w~~/AARclAA~/RgRnjVB-~ "Once you’ve finished reading this, please consider making a contribution of any amount to help me fund my campaign so I can get my message out to every voter!")**

Ever since I launched my campaign for President, I have read and heard my life described in every way imaginable. _**Today, I want you to hear my story in MY words.**_
---
| | | | [](http://post.spmailtechnol.com/f/a/JaiCnWsj_9Bbw3Attqdp9w~~/AARclAA~/RgRnjVB-~)
---
| I am the daughter of legal immigrants from a small, rural town in South Carolina. We were the only Indian family in our town. My father wore a turban as he still does to this day, and my mother wore a sari. No one knew who we were, what we were, or why we were there. But with each passing day, the community began to look beyond our skin color. They began to see my family for who we are: hard working people who held the same values they cherished. Gradually, those initial stares transformed into smiles and we shifted from being excluded to embraced. Not every day was perfect. But every day was better than the one before it.
---
After graduating from Clemson and working in the corporate world, I decided to take a job working for my family's business that my mother started in our living room when I was a child. I was frustrated when I saw how hard it was to make a dollar and how easy it was for government to take it away. When I voiced these frustrations to my mom, she gave me some wise advice which was: _" Don't complain. Do something about it." _
---
| | | So, that's exactly what I did and I decided to run for state legislature. But it wasn't easy. I ran against the longest-serving legislator in the state and hardly anyone thought I had a chance. I was polling at 15 percent a week before the primary. **But the people of South Carolina took a chance on me, and we won. ➡️**
---
| | [](http://post.spmailtechnol.com/f/a/JaiCnWsj_9Bbw3Attqdp9w~~/AARclAA~/RgRnjVB-~)
---
It was an honor to serve the people as a state legislator. I fought against the status quo and stood up for the people of my district. When I fought for government transparency by pushing to make sure important votes were on the record, my colleagues retaliated. They stripped me of my committees. So I decided to run for governor.

When I campaigned for governor, people didn't know who I was. I was polling in fourth place, with limited time until Election Day. I was the least funded and least known GOP candidate. But together, we defied expectations and won. Then, we made a difference in South Carolina by cutting taxes, creating thousands of jobs, and revitalizing our economy.

When I was nominated as Ambassador to the United Nations, people said I didn't have the experience. I proved them wrong. When I got to the UN, I took the "kick me" sign off our back. I told the world that America would have the backs of our allies, and for those who did not have our backs, we were taking names! The dictators, murderers, and thieves at the UN didn't know what hit them.

---
| [](http://post.spmailtechnol.com/f/a/JaiCnWsj_9Bbw3Attqdp9w~~/AARclAA~/RgRnjVB-~)
---

Now, I'm running for President because our country is heading down a path of doubt, division, and self-destruction. We need a leader who will rise to the occasion, offer solutions, and prioritize serving the people over the political class.

**[It would mean a lot to me if every single person _reading this today_ could send a donation of just $5 to help me keep my campaign momentum STRONG! >>](http://post.spmailtechnol.com/f/a/JaiCnWsj_9Bbw3Attqdp9w~~/AARclAA~/RgRnjVB-~ "It would mean a lot to me if every single person reading this today could send a donation of just $5 to help me keep my campaign momentum STRONG! >>")**

Your donation will not only show that my campaign is a force to be reckoned with, but it will also play a vital role in helping fund our campaign in the upcoming days.

**[Will you consider making a one-time donation of any amount today to show the strength of OUR movement?](http://post.spmailtechnol.com/f/a/JaiCnWsj_9Bbw3Attqdp9w~~/AARclAA~/RgRnjVB-~ "Will you consider making a one-time donation of any amount today to show the strength of OUR movement?")**

---
| | [RUSH SUPPORT TODAY](http://post.spmailtechnol.com/f/a/JaiCnWsj_9Bbw3Attqdp9w~~/AARclAA~/RgRnjVB-~)
---

Friend, throughout my life, I've been shaking up the status quo. I'm hoping to do the same as your next President. But in order to get there, **[I need your help- starting right now.](http://post.spmailtechnol.com/f/a/JaiCnWsj_9Bbw3Attqdp9w~~/AARclAA~/RgRnjVB-~ "I need your help – starting right now. ")**

Your contribution is what keeps this movement alive and thriving, so thank you for standing with me.

My very best,
---
| [](http://post.spmailtechnol.com/f/a/JaiCnWsj_9Bbw3Attqdp9w~~/AARclAA~/RgRnjVB-~)
---
Nikki Haley

My name is Nikki Haley. I want to tell you a bit about myself and why I'm running for President of the United States.

I'm running for President because my parents came to America more than 50 years ago - an America that was strong and proud, and full of opportunities. I want them to know that America again.

I'm running for President as a military spouse. My husband is deployed and I want him and his military brothers and sisters to know their sacrifice means something - that we do love this country.

I'm running for President for the future of our kids. I have a daughter who just got married and I saw how hard it was for her and her husband to buy a home. I'm doing this for my son who's a senior in college and shouldn't have to worry about saying things on a paper that he doesn't believe in just to get an A.

I'm running for my daughter, my son, and our future generations. I want them to experience the freedom and opportunity that the American Dream has to offer.

_**I 'm running for President because we have a country to save! **_

I've seen that even on our worst days, we are blessed to live in America. But I also know that under Biden's leadership, times are tough, our future is slipping, and America can be doing so much better.

**As governor, I was dubbed a "jobs governor"** because I slashed our unemployment rate, brought jobs back to our state, and shepherded in a successful economic recovery.

**At the UN I fought for America,** made sure our allies knew we had their backs and stood up to murderers and dictators to let them know that America was taking names.

I know how to make America strong and proud because I've done it before. **And I 'll do it as your next President. **

As President, I'll revitalize our economy, support small businesses, stop Washington's spending sprees, protect our border, champion school choice, and save America's future.
